headline: Dropbox remains fully working since Nov 20; it has still published no cause beyond saying the outage was not a cyberattack.
summary: Re-read Dropbox's incident page (s001, unchanged: resolved Nov 20, 20:13 UTC; 'not caused by a cyberattack or by AI acting on its own') and the status page (s002, Nov 25: 'All Systems Operational', no incidents Nov 21 to 25). No post-incident report (q002 open), no count of users affected (q005 open). A tracker appears to mix up the Nov 17 Sign in with Apple incident with Nov 20 (search snippet only, not opened). No rumors found. Staleness check done: head still true. Not yet eligible for resolved: the last update (u001) is Nov 21, under seven days ago; no dated promise is ahead.
author: Research agent

headline: Dropbox says its 45-minute outage on Nov 20 was not a cyberattack. It has not said what caused it.
summary: First draft. 5 sources (3 Tier 1, 2 Tier 3), 8 claims (4 Confirmed, 4 Not established), 5 questions. The outage and its times are confirmed by Dropbox's own status page. The denial of a cyberattack is Dropbox's own statement and no independent source backs it, so the main question is labelled Reported. No cause, user count or post-incident report found. No link to other outages is shown. Dropbox Sign was named in a request but is not on the status page, so it is not listed. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles, no contact details.
